digest.component_or_area: repository-wide quality audit and health assessment
propositions: Source repository contains 87 modules exceeding the 500-LOC documented target, with representative hotspots like compute() in next_batch.py and import_tickets() in import_ndjson.py combining multiple concerns in single functions; existing shrink-only ratchets prevent regression but high-complexity orchestration functions remain candidates for decomposition.

Global mypy passes all 440 source modules but a diagnostic --disallow-untyped-defs run found 687 errors; only rebar.graph and rebar.grounding packages currently enforce strict typing, so broad but shallow type coverage remains a medium-priority architectural debt.

Documentation contains navigation and example contradictions: README and user-guide teach --assignee alice while config docs require email/accountId; navigation routes to wrong targets; dependency and mypy configuration descriptions are stale relative to current topology.

Two reproducible test-environment failures exist: test_help_overview_coverage.py recursively decodes binary files under editor_assets/node_modules, and test_attestation_signing.py fails on shallow Git clones without historical objects; both have valid behavioral oracles but environment assumptions contradict CI sandbox conditions.

Python 3.11 xdist worker exhibits repeated flakiness in test_matching_guard_is_accepted with 'node down: Not properly terminated' after ~11.4k tests across four verified runs and two mirror runs, then passes unchanged, indicating teardown/serialization issues rather than patch behavior; issue is tracked but causes repeated CI gate failures and rerun latency.
